meta.title: Self-hosting guide | MAULT
meta.description: Run Mault on your own server with Docker Compose: Postgres, the API, the web app and the API docs, step by step.

hero.title: Run Mault on your own server
hero.description: Run Mault on your own hardware. Pick your setup and the guide shows only the steps you need. Progress is saved in this browser.

setup.label: Your setup
setup.title: Choose your setup
setup.description: Your choices are saved in the URL, so you can bookmark or share this guide.

compose.title: Docker Compose
compose.description: Any server you manage. Builds the stack from the repo.

coolify.title: Coolify
coolify.description: Runs the prebuilt images from GitHub Container Registry.

local.title: Built-in
local.description: Postgres and accounts run inside the stack. No outside services.

neon.title: Neon
neon.description: Hosted Postgres and Neon Auth. Adds email verification, password editing and social sign-in.

docker.text: Docker with Compose v2. This should print a version.

coolify.text: A Coolify instance with a server connected.

neonAccount.text: A Neon account. The free tier is enough.

node.text: Node.js, Git and pnpm on any machine, to run the Neon migrations. Corepack installs the right pnpm.

huggingface.text: Outbound access to huggingface.co for the scanner's model. Allowlist it in DNS blockers such as Pi-hole.

domain.text: Optional: a domain and an HTTPS reverse proxy for access outside your network.

configure.label: Configure
configure.title: Configure
configure.description: All settings live in one .env file in the repository root.

secrets.text: Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD, OWN_AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER, IMPERSONATION_SECRET and MONITOR_LINK_SECRET, each to its own random value.
secrets.note: Run the command once per secret.

secretsNeon.text: Set IMPERSONATION_SECRET and MONITOR_LINK_SECRET, each to its own random value.

webUrl.text: Set WEB_URL to the address people will open, without a trailing slash. Keep http://localhost:8080 for a single machine.

webUrlNeon.text: Set WEB_URL to the address people will open, without a trailing slash. The Neon example points at the dev server, so change it, for example to http://localhost:8080.

userAgent.text: Set CARD_API_USER_AGENT to a name unique to your install, such as MyMault/1.0. Sources block names that overuse them.

start.label: Start
start.title: Start the stack
start.description: Compose builds the images and starts every service.

up.text: Build and start in the background.

logs.text: Watch the server start. It runs the database migrations itself.

logsNeon.text: Watch the server start. It connects to your migrated Neon database.

ports.text: Web app :8080, API docs :8081, API :3001. Postgres listens only on 127.0.0.1:5433.

portsNeon.text: Web app :8080, API docs :8081, API :3001. The bundled Postgres starts but isn't used.

firstRun.label: First sign-in
firstRun.title: Create your account
firstRun.description: Sign up, then add a game to match scans against.

signUp.text: Open your WEB_URL and sign up. The first account becomes platform admin with a Home organization.
signUp.note: Email verification, password editing, multi-session management and social sign-in need Neon.

signUpNeon.text: Open your WEB_URL, sign up and create your organization.

adminNeon.text: Make yourself platform admin in Neon's SQL editor.

game.text: In /app/admin, add a game in the Games Manager and run its sync. Scans can't match until one has synced.

admins.text: Optional: make another user platform admin. There's no screen for it yet.

prices.label: Prices
prices.title: Schedule price sync
prices.description: Prices come from TCGplayer, Cardmarket and Card Kingdom. Sync once a day, never more often: sources block installs that poll harder.

cron.text: Add this with crontab -e, replacing /opt/mault with your docker-compose.yml folder.
cron.note: Failed runs aren't retried. The next daily run catches up.

firstPull.text: After your first game sync, run the command once by hand. Cards have no price until then. Logs go to /var/log/mault-prices.log.

coolify.text: In Scheduled Tasks, add this command with container server and frequency 0 4 * * *.
coolify.note: After your first game sync, run it once from the server terminal. Failed runs aren't retried.

optional.label: Extras
optional.title: Optional features
optional.description: Each stays off until its variables are set. Restart or redeploy after changes.

discord.text: Discord bot: set DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_CLIENT_ID and BOT_API_SECRET, then start with the bot profile.

discordCoolify.text: Discord bot: set DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_CLIENT_ID and BOT_API_SECRET, then redeploy.

storage.text: File storage: point SCAN_IMAGE_BUCKET and the AWS_* variables at any S3-compatible bucket. Otherwise files are kept in Postgres.

email.text: Email: set RESEND_API_KEY and RESEND_FROM_EMAIL for password resets and invites. Otherwise invites are link-only.

wifi.text: Wi-Fi sorters: set SORTER_LINK_URL (or API_URL) to an address the sorter board can reach.

maintain.label: Maintenance
maintain.title: Updates and backups
maintain.description: Stay current and protect your data.

migrateNeon.text: Before each update, pull the latest code and run the Neon migrations.

update.text: Pull and rebuild. Migrations run on start-up.

updateCoolify.text: Redeploy. Coolify fetches the latest compose file and pulls the current image for your tag.

backupCoolify.text: Keep the mault-postgres volume across redeploys and back it up regularly.

backupNeon.text: Neon holds your data. Use its restore window and branches as backups.

secrets.text: Don't rotate secrets casually. A new OWN_AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER signs everyone out, and changing POSTGRES_PASSWORD doesn't update the existing database.

coolify.label: Coolify
coolify.title: Deploy with Coolify
coolify.description: Coolify runs the published images, so nothing builds on your server.

compose.text: Create + New > Public Repository with this URL, branch master, build pack Docker Compose and compose file /docker-compose-coolify.yml.

images.text: These images are pulled. Set MAULT_IMAGE_TAG (for example v1.2.3) to pin a version. The default is latest.

env.text: In the environment, set WEB_URL to your public origin without a trailing slash, and give POSTGRES_PASSWORD, IMPERSONATION_SECRET, OWN_AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER and MONITOR_LINK_SECRET each its own random value.
env.note: Leave VITE_API_URL and the Neon variables empty.

envNeon.text: In the environment, set these values, WEB_URL (no trailing slash) and your Neon values. Also give POSTGRES_PASSWORD, IMPERSONATION_SECRET, OWN_AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER and MONITOR_LINK_SECRET each its own random value, since the compose file requires them.
envNeon.note: Neon only accepts encrypted connections, hence DATABASE_SSL=true.

domain.text: Assign your domain to the web service on port 80, such as https://mault.example.com:80.

deploy.text: Deploy. The bot stays idle until its Discord variables are set.

neon.label: Neon
neon.title: Set up Neon
neon.description: Neon hosts the database, sign-in and file storage. The containers never migrate Neon, so you run the migrations yourself.

project.text: Create a project at console.neon.tech and run this in its SQL editor.

auth.text: Enable Neon Auth (Dashboard > Auth) before migrating.

urls.text: Copy the pooled connection string (DATABASE_URL), the auth URL (NEON_AUTH_URL and VITE_NEON_AUTH_URL) and the Data API URL (VITE_NEON_DATA_API_URL).

storage.text: Create a bucket in Neon's object storage and copy its name, S3 endpoint, region and keys into SCAN_IMAGE_BUCKET, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, AWS_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.

clone.text: On a machine with Node.js, clone the repository, copy the Neon example config and set DATABASE_URL.
